concepts.name: Project
concepts.definition: The single existing software project served by a Project Harness, potentially spanning several repositories.

concepts.name: Repository
concepts.definition: A version-controlled code repository belonging to the target project. Several repositories can belong to the same Project without requiring separate Project Harnesses.

concepts.name: Native Paseo
concepts.definition: The host product that owns native projects, workspaces, profiles, agent sessions and their management interfaces. Project Harness references those resources and adds its own work coordination and improvement capabilities.

concepts.name: Workspace
concepts.definition: A native Paseo execution context referenced by harness work and associated with the project's code and runtime resources.

concepts.name: Onboarding
concepts.definition: The initial configuration and usage guidance provided through native Paseo conversation before the user starts the harness build stage.

concepts.name: Readiness Report
concepts.definition: A scoped assessment of required checks, blockers, optional gaps and evidence against identified configuration and dependency revisions. Its conclusion concerns a named build or launch stage rather than general project competence.

concepts.name: Build Readiness
concepts.definition: The condition in which the required project context, configuration, capabilities, authority and limits are sufficient for the intended initial harness build.

concepts.name: Launch Readiness
concepts.definition: The condition in which the Project Orchestrator's required configuration, references and tools are valid and its handover is saved, sufficient to offer user-initiated launch.

concepts.name: Operational Verification
concepts.definition: An evidence-based demonstration that a selected representative project task meets its applicable criteria within a stated capability scope.

concepts.name: Handover
concepts.definition: Durable context and continuity information for the next responsible agent session or lifecycle stage, including relevant work, decisions, revisions and evidence. It supports continuity without itself conferring authority or replacing saved execution state.

concepts.name: Orchestrator Session Binding
concepts.definition: A revisioned association between a persistent orchestrator responsibility and its current native Agent Session, with distinguishable history across session replacements.

concepts.name: Orchestrator Responsibility
concepts.definition: The persistent responsibility for either project-work orchestration or harness engineering, independent of which Agent Session currently carries it.

concepts.name: Capability
concepts.definition: An ability actually supported by a host, provider, tool or integration that is needed to fulfill the requested work contract. Availability of that ability does not establish permission to use it.

concepts.name: Authority
concepts.definition: The scope granted to a caller for making decisions and causing actions on behalf of the project or harness. A role name, catalog entry or accessible tool does not by itself grant that scope.

concepts.name: Permission
concepts.definition: Authorization for a particular action under the applicable allow, ask or deny policy and native enforcement. Approval for one action does not by itself broaden standing authority.

concepts.name: Effective Authority
concepts.definition: The authority usable for a particular action after the caller's granted scope, parent Assignment restrictions, current policies and revocations are taken into account.

concepts.name: Resource Limit
concepts.definition: An applicable ceiling on shared harness execution resources, such as concurrency, elapsed work time or measurable spending. The limit's scope includes relevant orchestrators, workers and consultations.

concepts.name: Delegation Mode
concepts.definition: A permitted way of using an Agent Definition under a caller's Delegation Policy: Delegate, Consult or Workflow. A mode describes the use of the definition without independently granting tool permissions or further delegation.

concepts.name: Delegate
concepts.definition: The permitted-use mode in which a specific portion of work is assigned to an agent and its Outcome is returned.

concepts.name: Consult
concepts.definition: The permitted-use mode for requesting advice, findings or options while the caller retains responsibility for carrying out the work. It grants no authority to modify project code or push, merge or release changes.

concepts.name: Workflow Mode
concepts.definition: The permitted-use mode in which an Agent Definition can participate in a workflow coordinated by code. It does not by itself authorize the worker to start workflows or delegate further.

concepts.name: Agent Procedure
concepts.definition: The role-associated method for performing a kind of agent work, described by its entry instructions and required result. It is distinct from a running workflow or the Skill package that carries guidance.

concepts.name: Entry Skill
concepts.definition: A Skill required as the entry guidance for an Agent Procedure and included in the Agent Definition selected for that procedure.

concepts.name: Result Contract
concepts.definition: The requirements for the content, structure and supporting evidence of returned work. Satisfying its structural requirements alone does not establish that the work meets its evaluation criteria.

concepts.name: Core Operating Rules
concepts.definition: The always-applicable rules governing authority, evidence and quality across agent work, independent of the selected task-specific Principles.

concepts.name: Principle Selection
concepts.definition: The policy for selecting task-specific Principles using Automatic, Fixed or Hybrid selection while retaining the Core Operating Rules.

concepts.name: Configuration Revision
concepts.definition: An identified version of harness-owned configuration, distinguishable from earlier and later edits. Existing work retains its selected configuration rather than silently adopting a later edit.

concepts.name: Effective Configuration
concepts.definition: The resolved native profile and harness-owned method and policy selections identified for a particular work execution. It records what that work selected rather than a second editable source of native provider settings.

concepts.name: Pinned Revision
concepts.definition: A particular revision retained as the identified basis for a work execution. Its use carries the source or retained-content evidence appropriate to that resource, without implying that an external mutable Skill has been snapshotted.

concepts.name: Source Drift
concepts.definition: A detected difference between a resource's current source or dependency identity and the version previously checked or selected for work.

concepts.name: Workflow Pattern
concepts.definition: A reusable structure for coordinating workflow steps and bounded agent decisions, with a contract for sequencing, routing, parallel work, dynamic work division or iterative evaluation.

concepts.name: Prompt Chaining
concepts.definition: A Workflow Pattern in which the checked output of one step supplies a compatible input to a later step.

concepts.name: Routing
concepts.definition: A Workflow Pattern in which a bounded decision selects among the branches permitted by the workflow.

concepts.name: Parallelization
concepts.definition: A Workflow Pattern with branches that can execute concurrently under shared admission limits and an explicit Join Policy.

concepts.name: Orchestrator-Workers
concepts.definition: A Workflow Pattern in which work portions are determined dynamically within a selected template, required capabilities and resource limits.

concepts.name: Evaluator-Optimizer
concepts.definition: A Workflow Pattern in which evaluation feedback guides revisions of a result within defined criteria, iteration limits and stopping conditions.

concepts.name: Workflow Step
concepts.definition: A step in a Workflow Definition that may be visited more than once in a Workflow Run. It identifies a position in the flow rather than a particular execution.

concepts.name: Step Run
concepts.definition: An identified visit by a Workflow Run to a Workflow Step, potentially containing several Attempts for technical retries. Returning to the same step after a result-revision cycle creates a new Step Run.

concepts.name: Execution Plan
concepts.definition: The selected execution structure for a particular Workflow Run, including recorded dynamic expansions permitted by its chosen definition and policies.

concepts.name: Join Policy
concepts.definition: The rule identifying which branches to await, when their set is closed and the conditions for aggregating or continuing a workflow step. It distinguishes required-result availability from quality assessment and defines branch-failure handling.
disallowedTerms: trạng thái toàn bộ Work Item

concepts.name: Stop Condition
concepts.definition: A workflow rule identifying when an evaluation-and-revision loop must end, whether because its criteria are met or further permitted evaluation or revision is exhausted.

concepts.name: Feedback
concepts.definition: Sourced information about execution or evaluation that can inform diagnosis, revision or improvement.

concepts.name: Trigger
concepts.definition: A time, event or manual condition under which a Job or other work target becomes eligible for activation.

concepts.name: Trigger Binding
concepts.definition: A revisioned association between an identified activation source and a harness work target, together with the supported delivery and admission policies.

concepts.name: Source Event
concepts.definition: An identified source object or change normalized from an integration for downstream processing, with identity independent of the time it was polled.

concepts.name: Work Delivery
concepts.definition: The tracked handoff of a source activation or change to durable harness work, whose acceptance is distinct from execution of that work.

concepts.name: Source Cursor
concepts.definition: A committed marker of progress in an integration source stream. It records source progress without by itself establishing downstream work delivery.

concepts.name: Code Job Handler
concepts.definition: Registered, versioned code that performs a Job using validated inputs and reports its result and relevant source progress or evidence.

concepts.name: Overlap Policy
concepts.definition: The per-Job rule for activations that arrive while an earlier execution is still running, allowing skipped new work, one queued execution or bounded parallel execution.

concepts.name: Missed Occurrence Policy
concepts.definition: The per-Job rule for due occurrences missed while execution was unavailable, allowing skips, one coalesced execution or bounded catch-up.

concepts.name: Integration
concepts.definition: An authorized connection and adapter for an external task or code-review source used by the harness, with Backlog tasks and GitLab merge requests and comments in V1.

concepts.name: Paseo Cadence
concepts.definition: The native Paseo-owned timing, timezone and enablement of an agent schedule or heartbeat referenced by the harness.

concepts.name: Tracked Operation
concepts.definition: A durably tracked request for an action whose acceptance, progress and actual effects can remain distinguishable across interruption or uncertain responses.

concepts.name: Operation Intent
concepts.definition: A durable description of an intended action and its correlation to the responsible operation, distinguishable from evidence that the action actually took effect.

concepts.name: Receipt
concepts.definition: An acknowledgement that the particular acceptance or change declared by an interface has been durably recorded. Its meaning is limited to that declared stage rather than proving downstream execution or readiness.

concepts.name: Idempotency Key
concepts.definition: A caller- and operation-scoped request identity used to recognize repeated submissions of the same intent. In this design, matching payloads refer back to the prior receipt, while a conflicting payload is a conflict.

concepts.name: Reconciliation
concepts.definition: Assessment of recorded intent and observations from the resource owner to establish what happened and whether work can safely continue.

concepts.name: Execution Admission
concepts.definition: The code-controlled decision permitting new execution under the current pause state, resource limits, required capabilities and effective authority.

concepts.name: Retry
concepts.definition: Another permitted execution after a technical failure, distinct from a revision in response to quality feedback. A retry of step execution creates a new Attempt within the same Step Run.

concepts.name: Timeout
concepts.definition: The expiry of the permitted waiting period for a response or result. It does not establish that the worker stopped or that its effects were undone.

concepts.name: Cancellation
concepts.definition: A request to stop selected work, distinguishable from confirmation that the stop has taken effect. Prior effects, artifacts and history remain relevant to reconciliation.

concepts.name: Interruption
concepts.definition: A disruption of execution or communication, such as disconnection, process reload or crash, that can leave the state of work or effects uncertain.

concepts.name: Run Timer
concepts.definition: A durable due-time associated with existing work, a step or an Attempt, whose meaning remains tied to that execution context.

concepts.name: Operation Journal
concepts.definition: A durable history of execution or operation intent, progress and observations that supports reconciliation and continuation after interruption.

concepts.name: Outbox
concepts.definition: Pending delivery records retained with local source progress so delivery can be resumed or reconciled without losing an accepted change.

concepts.name: Lease
concepts.definition: A time-bounded claim on dispatch or operation responsibility that does not itself prove an earlier holder can no longer cause effects.

concepts.name: Fencing
concepts.definition: Enforcement that rejects commands from superseded responsibility holders or execution attempts at the boundary where effects are accepted.

concepts.name: Observed State
concepts.definition: The state of a resource supported by an observation at an identified time and scope, including uncertainty when a required fact has not been established.

concepts.name: Desired State
concepts.definition: The requested target state of controlled work or a resource, distinct from what has actually been observed.

concepts.name: Unknown
concepts.definition: A qualification indicating that a required fact has not been established by available evidence.

concepts.name: Hypothesis
concepts.definition: A testable proposed explanation or expected effect of an improvement, informed by feedback and observations.

concepts.name: Experiment
concepts.definition: A planned investigation of a hypothesis using identified work, conditions and evaluation evidence. It concerns how a proposed effect is investigated, rather than the Candidate change itself.

concepts.name: Regression
concepts.definition: An evidence-supported worsening relative to an identified reference and applicable criteria under sufficiently comparable conditions.

concepts.name: Fix-forward
concepts.definition: Repair of a contained failure through a subsequent corrective change while the affected capability is blocked and relevant state is retained for diagnosis. It requires a functioning diagnostic and repair path and does not itself restore data or permit continued use of the known-broken capability.

concepts.name: Recovery Operation
concepts.definition: An operation to restore runnable harness code through an independent recovery path, using a release compatible with current data and retained work.

concepts.name: Recovery Executable
concepts.definition: The small recovery program packaged with the plugin but able to run outside its subprocess, including while that plugin cannot boot.

concepts.name: Backup
concepts.definition: A saved copy of data whose readability has been verified for the relevant preservation purpose. Its existence does not establish successful system restoration or authorize replacing current data.

concepts.name: Data Compatibility
concepts.definition: The ability of a selected release or recovery program to operate safely with the current data format, retained work and relevant recorded effects.

concepts.name: Check Plan
concepts.definition: The candidate-specific selection of required and justified additional checks, with the affected scope, inputs, limits and reasons identified.

concepts.name: Check Result
concepts.definition: The sourced outcome of a particular check on an identified Candidate and relevant inputs and environment. A post-activation health result also concerns the particular runtime instance and operation checked.

concepts.name: Evaluation Dataset
concepts.definition: An identified, frozen collection of evaluation inputs with their provenance and scope, retained as an Artifact for particular evaluations.

concepts.name: Evaluation Suite
concepts.definition: An identified set of evaluation cases with the criteria and grading arrangements used to assess them.

concepts.name: Evaluation Environment
concepts.definition: The identified conditions relevant to an Evaluation Trial, including applicable program, model, Skill, tool and grader revisions that affect comparability.

concepts.name: Metric Availability
concepts.definition: The availability of an actual measurement for a Metric in a particular observation scope. A real numeric zero is distinct from data that is missing or cannot be measured.

concepts.name: Upstream Contribution
concepts.definition: Separately authorized work to extract, verify and propose reusable harness improvements to an upstream project. Its acceptance is independent of applying improvements locally.

concepts.name: Decision
concepts.definition: A recorded answer to a Decision Request, retained with the relevant work context and revision. It resolves that issue without automatically expanding standing authority.

concepts.name: Deadline
concepts.definition: A time boundary for waiting for a response or for the eligibility of an execution step. Reaching it can trigger timeout handling without proving that work or external effects have stopped.

concepts.name: Evaluation Case
concepts.definition: A defined evaluation task or input situation with applicable criteria, used as an individual case within an evaluation suite.

concepts.name: Attribution Policy
concepts.definition: The rule associating recorded costs with traceable work or subjects while distinguishing shared and unmeasured portions. Unallocated shared costs remain separate and are counted once in totals; estimated allocations state their method and data source.

concepts.name: Instructions

concepts.name: Learned Knowledge
concepts.definition: Reusable observations or lessons retained with their sources, scope and degree of certainty. It is distinct from authoritative project requirements and the recorded state of execution.

constraints.text: Exactly two persistent orchestrator responsibilities; onboarding is a setup helper, not a third.
One project, potentially multiple repositories, one plugin; no multi-project platform.
Startup at each stage is explicitly initiated by user; complete/check only opens the next permitted action. Existing role normally opens existing Session.
Build-ready, launch-ready and representative task verification are distinct scoped claims. Unknown mandatory check blocks the dependent stage.
Handover is saved outside transcript and does not replace a checkpoint or itself authorize dispatch. Dependency changes require recheck.
Native owns profiles/provider/options/workspaces/sessions; harness stores refs and required snapshots, no duplicate active editor/store.
Profile must exist before definition reference. Missing/deleted configured ref blocks rather than silently selecting another.

Fallback only in configured order for unavailable/rate-limited candidates satisfying capability/authority/contract/budget; never bypass deny, missing required skill or ambiguous effect reconciliation.
Explicit Skill name/source, no isolation/fork/monkey patch requirement; entry Skill absent blocks procedure.
Auto/fixed/hybrid retain core operating rules; fixed may be empty, hybrid preserves mandatory selection.
Catalog membership is not authorization. Policy is per orchestrator and permits modes per definition.
Consult grants no project write/push/merge/release; native enforcement is necessary, prompt is insufficient.
Worker delegation defaults off; permitted child authority is subset of parent Assignment; shared admission/budget applies to both orchestrators and all modes.
Permission expansion applies to new work; revocation checked before next action. Stop/replace unsupported sessions; occurred effects are not undone.
A Work Item has zero/many Runs; completed Run does not automatically resolve request; request-scope criteria/evidence required.

A Session can receive several Assignments over time, each retaining its selected configuration and Outcome. Genuine retry/fallback redispatch uses a new Assignment even on the same Session (K62); uncertain responses and continued Turns retain the current identity (K63). Session concurrency is not generalized from fixture behavior.

Technical retry creates a new Attempt in the same Step Run; quality-driven correction is a Quality Iteration and a return to the step creates a new Step Run. Rejection before admission records a blocker without creating an Attempt.
Five composable/nestable patterns; dynamic workers and loops are supported. Runtime controls structure/invariants; agent choices remain constrained.

Route picks a valid branch; parallel requires an explicit join/failure policy (K53–K55); optimizer requires criteria, feedback and bounded stopping. Aggregate Outcome content and result reuse follow K56/K57.
Schema correctness, Turn end, idle, actual Outcome and scoped Verdict are distinct; no automatic pass.
Work pins definition/criteria/config; edits affect new work, migration only at compatible recorded Checkpoint. External Skill drift blocks next affected step for replan.
Once/interval/cron with timezone; overlap skip/queue-one/bounded parallel; missed skip/coalesce/bounded catch-up. Host off stops all local jobs; no cloud substitute.
Each schedule has one data owner; native cadence is not replayed by a second scheduler. Unsupported evidence-dependent native policy must be reported.

Unchanged code poll calls no agent. The handler reports source progress/events; the owning runtime commits cursor/events/outbox and reconciles receipts using stable source/change identities. A committed cursor alone is not a Work Delivery receipt; external effects are not promised exactly-once.
Occurrence may skip/coalesce/queue; manual Job Run needs no Occurrence; successful Job Run need not create Work Item or Workflow Run.
Same scoped request key/payload returns receipt; different payload conflicts. Durable acceptance is distinct from dispatch/effect/readiness.
Ambiguous native create/send outcome requires reconcile before retry; no unconditional exactly-once external effect claim.

Replacing Session saves handover, stops old-role dispatch, reconciles work and transfers role; stale commands rejected, history/workers retained by default. Native bypass requires actual enforcement or stop old session.
Timeout/cancel/interruption do not prove worker stop or effect reversal; late results retained without overwriting current attempt.
Pause blocks new admission; desired state differs from observed worker stop. Old attempt timers must not affect new attempts.
Daily retro can conclude no change; quality/requirements mandatory, cost/time/intervention optimization does not override them.
Passing evaluation grants no activation authority. allow/ask/deny checked; one approval does not rewrite ask policy.
Full plugin self-update covers UI/runtime/schema/resources/jobs/integrations. Pause only affected work; unknown impact defers activation.
Fast/Deep selected by risk; code enforces mandatory checks and limits; no default full nightly suite. Pending/failed checks are not pass.
Mandatory pre/post activation checks must pass. Activated but failed health is not verified; contain affected functions, unknown scope pauses all new admission.
Single activation at a time; unrelated activations wait during failed post-check while candidates can be prepared.
Reuse checks only same candidate/check/relevant inputs/environment. Post-activation health is fresh per runtime instance/operation.
Failures meeting the four containment/repair conditions in K61 use Fix-forward; unbootable/lost-self-repair uses independent compatible recovery. No automatic old database restore.
Backup required before incompatible/hard-to-reverse data changes; verified-readable is not proof of whole-system restore. Recovery executor protected within its operation.

Target/actual active/operation-scoped recovery are roles of Release, not subclasses. Selected target may fail; actual active may be null; last verified is not automatically current-data-compatible recovery.
Metric value zero differs from missing/unavailable. Record provenance/units/scope; never fabricate cost or causality.
Controlled comparisons need compatible inputs/criteria/conditions/grader and provenance; inconclusive is valid. Operational difference alone is not causal improvement.
Saved View stores query/display configuration, not frozen data or immutable Verdict; reopening can yield new observations.
Local improvement independent of upstream acceptance; extracting/testing/PR requires separate authority; no automatic publication.
Native chat is main interaction, no mandatory task forms/composer/router. Chat/panel share validation, authority/revision and owner interfaces.
Backlog tasks and GitLab merge requests/comments are real V1 integration requirements, not fixture proof; code adapters separate from workflow.
Both Claude and Codex must satisfy Skills/Principles/result/resume/fallback and native authority requirements; fixture selection is not evidence.
Context includes necessary task/inputs/decisions/criteria/pinned configuration, not automatic full transcript; more context does not widen access.
Missing capability creates deduplicated linked engineering request; unresolved authority/resource need escalates to user, independent work continues.
Secrets values are not in chat/export/log; use appropriate references. Caller principal/host/workspace/role is bound by trusted adapter, not self-declared payload.

A Workflow Step is a definition position. Each visit within a Workflow Run has a distinct Step Run; technical retry creates a new Attempt within that Step Run, while returning after quality correction creates a new Step Run. Admission/dispatch follow the separately accepted K52 rule.

Rejection before admission creates no Attempt. Once execution is permitted, record an Attempt before dispatch. Lost dispatch response retains that Attempt for reconciliation; the record alone proves neither worker start nor completion. Missing response is not proof of no execution.

Default join is all-required: valid results from every required branch are needed before aggregate evaluation. Result availability does not imply a passing quality Verdict. Other join/failure behavior must be declared; K54 defines dynamic closure and K55 defines the default required-branch failure behavior.

A dynamic branch set accepts only validated, recorded additions within policy while open. Successful join requires explicit closure and all required results; completion of currently known workers alone is insufficient. Work discovered after closure is recorded as another expansion or processing iteration without silently mutating the set being aggregated.

If a required branch suffers terminal technical failure after its retry allowance, default to letting other already-running branches finish within their admitted limits and preserve every branch Outcome. The aggregate cannot proceed as though all required results were available. Stopping other branches immediately requires explicit fail-fast policy. A valid review reporting quality defects is distinct from failure to obtain the required report.

An aggregate Outcome records accomplished work with branch Outcome/output references; errors, missing required results and remaining work; and Artifacts/Evidence with relevant input/criteria versions. Its scoped quality Verdict remains separate. Aggregation preserves source results/history even when the request is unresolved.

A completed branch result may be reused only after checking that relevant code, review scope and criteria remain applicable and its Evidence is accessible. Changes require impact assessment to determine what must rerun. New processing records the reused result and source without rewriting old history. This workflow/review reuse rule does not relax K37: release checks remain same-candidate and post-activation health is fresh.

Deep path is mandatory for changes to protective state persistence/recovery, duplicate external-effect prevention, authority enforcement, activation/recovery and self-repair mechanisms, including authority-expanding configuration. UI/Skill content/schedule edits may use Fast path only with demonstrated narrow impact and unchanged protection. Code detection is still engineering work.

Evidence is selected by change goal: bug reproduction and related behavior for fixes; representative and prior failure cases in the affected scope for agent/workflow behavior changes; sufficiently comparable Baseline/Candidate inputs, criteria and conditions for improvement claims. No universal fixed repeat count is set. Insufficient evidence is Inconclusive; release mandatory checks still apply.

Attribute measured costs directly only with traceable source. Keep measured but unallocated costs shared and count each cost once in totals; distinguish direct, shared and unmeasured data. Future estimated allocations must state method/source. This does not define parallel elapsed-time attribution or causal outcome credit.

Fix-forward requires all four: evidenced impact scope; ability to block affected work/external effects; readable necessary state with relevant integrity checks passing; and a working diagnostic/repair path with needed authority. Otherwise pause admission at the necessary scope and reconcile first. Unknown scope still halts all new admission; unbootable/lost-self-repair uses independent current-data-compatible recovery, without automatic old-data restore.

An Assignment is one specific allocation to an agent. A permitted technical retry/fallback that actually redispatches the work creates a new Assignment and a new Attempt within the same Step Run, even if it reuses the recipient Session. The new allocation records its predecessor; an issued allocation is not silently rebound to a fallback Session. Code-only Attempts need not create Assignments.

Lost create/send response retains the current Attempt/Assignment for reconciliation. Clarification or continuation through several Turns does not itself create a new allocation. Late results remain attached to the original Assignment/Attempt without overwriting current execution; reuse requires K57. Replacing the orchestrator Session does not itself cancel or rebind running worker Assignments.

Versioned instructions selected by role/definition are combined with applicable shared rules and Assignment context. Native profile options and method/result contracts retain their owners; this does not establish universal native instruction inventory or precedence.

New worker work uses a fresh Session by default; clarification/continued Turns of the same Assignment retain its Session. Reuse for different work requires an explicit compatibility policy. This does not change GA01 retry/redispatch identities or orchestrator Open/Replace.

Learned notes retain source, scope and certainty outside transcript/execution history, with Harness/Project logical scope and authority-aware retrieval. They do not become authoritative requirements, criteria or grants. Knowledge owns their lifecycle; Work retains execution/context snapshots.

Contested or source-drifted notes keep qualified history and are excluded from automatic default loading until applicability recheck records a new conclusion/revision. Drift alone does not prove a false lesson; this does not invalidate authoritative requirements or force every note through Deep release.

Orchestrators record structured cycle disposition through owner MCP Tools; runtime checks durable state before continue/wait. Individual events/results survive coalesced wake while busy; no marker/text oracle, per-callback interrupt or extra orchestrator is implied. Cycle/Turn completion is not Work completion.

Useful notes can be recorded during existing work without a mandatory lesson or extra LLM Turn per task. Daily retro curates with outcomes/metrics and proposes evidence-backed candidates when justified; urgent blockers need not wait for daily.

Task-specific composition from registered blocks/roles/Tools validates contracts/structure/authority/bounds and pins its plan before execution, without plugin release. Reusable registration or persistent code/Tool/Skill/operating behavior changes require candidate/check/activation; arbitrary unverified generated code is not a bypass.

The base ships versioned Onboarding/Engineering instructions/definitions, starter specialist presets, workflow blocks/templates and validation/eval fixtures. Onboarding binds existing native profiles/installed methods; Engineering adapts them. Five responsibility presets are not a mandatory pipeline, pre-spawned workers or universal capability proof.

Fresh install/Onboarding does not start an LLM loop or real external polling. Enabled daily retro is eligible after user Spawn Engineering with bindings/cadence/authority ready; code polling needs connection/filter/cadence/enabled. Restart preserves disabled state without automatic Spawn/Replace; authorized recurring runs need no per-run approval.

Explicit durable orchestrator Pause blocks controlled automatic wake/new admission until authorized Resume via the shared Work owner Interface. Native Stop only requests Turn interruption; canceled/idle does not establish human Pause, and event/reload/Open Session does not Resume. Native cadence coordination must show pending/confirmed truthfully.

Pause affects only that orchestrator automatic wake/new admissions/progression. Running workers/results/evidence/events, independent enabled ingestion jobs and the other orchestrator are retained. Worker cancellation, job disable and whole-kit controls have separate scope; revoked authority and existing effect uncertainty remain applicable.

questions.answer: A Session can receive multiple Assignments over time; concurrency is not decided here. Each actual permitted retry/fallback redispatch creates a new Assignment, even on the same Session, with separate selected configuration, recipient and Outcome history. Technical retry uses a new Attempt in the same Step Run. Continued Turns or uncertain response retain identity. Run aggregation references branch Outcomes/evidence and a separate scoped Verdict; eligible prior results may be reused under K57 without overwriting history or automatically resolving the Work Item.

runtimeEvidence.note: Prototype identities/controls checked; no production persistence, dispatch/evaluation/compatibility probe.

questions.question: Lỗi kỹ thuật, phản hồi chất lượng và thiếu quyền tạo Attempt, Iteration hay blocked state?
questions.answer: Accepted: each visit has its own Step Run; technical retry creates a new Attempt in that Step Run, while quality-driven return creates a new Step Run. Rejection before admission creates no Attempt. Once permitted, record the Attempt before dispatch; lost response retains it for reconciliation and proves neither start nor non-execution. Quality Iteration remains distinct. Accepted GA01: an actual agent-work redispatch also creates a new Assignment, even when the Session is reused; continued Turns or a lost response do not.

runtimeEvidence.note: Design requirement and conceptual answer only; no complete production behavior proof.

questions.question: Năm pattern nối tiếp/lồng/song song nhau có Step identity và kiểu đầu vào/đầu ra thế nào?
questions.answer: All five patterns compose recursively with validated input/output, branch and stop rules. Authoring is versioned code, not a required graph editor. Accepted identity: each visit to a Workflow Step within a Workflow Run creates a distinct Step Run; technical retries remain Attempts of that visit.

runtimeEvidence.note: Design requirement and conceptual answer only; no complete production behavior proof.

questions.question: Parallel join biết chờ nhánh nào khi có worker động và một nhánh lỗi?
questions.answer: Accepted: dynamically added branches are validated and recorded within policy until the set is closed; successful join requires closure and valid results from all required branches. Completion of existing workers alone is insufficient. Required technical failure after retry allowance keeps the join from proceeding; by default already-running branches finish within admitted limits and each Outcome is retained. Fail-fast/quorum require explicit declaration. Post-closure discoveries use another recorded expansion or processing iteration. A valid report identifying quality defects is not the same as missing required output.

runtimeEvidence.note: Design requirement and conceptual answer only; no complete production behavior proof.

questions.question: Evaluator-optimizer dừng khi đạt, hết budget hoặc inconclusive khác nhau thế nào?
questions.answer: Optimizer stops by applicable criteria or a bounded stopping condition; budget exhaustion and Inconclusive do not mean success. Stop Condition and Outcome meanings are accepted; exact wire statuses and result schemas belong in the execution protocol rather than a new glossary definition.

decisions.title: Approve local owner vocabulary and canonical English names
decisions.recommendation: Accepted canonical English names, concise definitions and documented owners for the reviewed 96 IDs; preserve aliases/anchors and keep 23 general terms as contextual references.
decisions.alternatives: Approve coherent groups; or request specific semantic changes. Do not run per-label translation rounds.
decisions.resolved: Explicit current confirmation: Q1 at T3 P2720 was answered ok at P2722 on 2026-10-23. The 96 reviewed English names, definitions and owners are accepted; preserve aliases/anchors and 23 contextual references. Earlier P2367 scope ambiguity is retained in history. This confirms D01, not all graph cardinalities, schemas, runtime proof or session closure.

decisions.title: Execution identity on loop/retry/rejection
decisions.recommendation: Accepted: one Step Run per visit, new Attempt for technical retry in that visit, new Step Run on quality-driven return. Rejection before admission creates no Attempt; record an admitted Attempt before dispatch; retain it on lost response and reconcile.
decisions.alternatives: A single mutable Step Run across loop visits and treating a missing response as proof of no execution were not selected. Durable transaction/correlation/reconciliation mechanics and production proof remain engineering work, not open product decisions in D02.
decisions.resolved: Workflow Step/Step Run names and identity accepted in the first round; admission/dispatch boundary accepted in the following Q1. D02 is semantically resolved. This is not runtime proof.

decisions.title: Join, aggregation and late-result contract
decisions.recommendation: Accepted: all-required with explicit dynamic closure; preserve bounded results after required failure; aggregate records branch outputs, failures/missing work and versioned supporting material; quality Verdict stays separate. Reuse checks applicability/evidence and records provenance without changing prior history. Release checks retain K37 restrictions.
decisions.alternatives: Implicit closed-set mutation, skipping failed required branches, partial results as automatic success and unverified reuse were not selected. Explicit quorum/fail-fast remain available. Work Item resolution continues to require scoped criteria/evidence (K15).
decisions.resolved: All semantic choices in D03 are resolved by the successive accepted reviews, ending with aggregate content and reuse eligibility. Exact schemas, dependency/cache identity, reconciliation and live proof remain engineering work, not open product choices in D03.

decisions.title: Risk and recovery eligibility
decisions.recommendation: Accepted: mandatory Deep triggers for protective mechanisms and authority expansion; narrow changes may stay Fast with protection unchanged. Fix-forward requires evidenced scope, enforceable containment, readable/integrity-checked state and a working authorized repair path. Otherwise pause/reconcile; independent compatible recovery applies to unbootable/lost-self-repair cases.
decisions.alternatives: Continuing known-broken capability, assuming containment without evidence or restoring old data automatically were not selected. Exact probes, code detection, effect enforcement and compatibility/recovery mechanics remain engineering work.
decisions.resolved: Risk triggers were accepted in SRC315, and the four conjunctive Fix-forward conditions in SRC320 close the remaining semantic choice. D04 is resolved; native enforcement and live behavior are not proved by the interview.

decisions.title: Evaluation and measurement contracts
decisions.recommendation: Accepted: goal-specific minimum evidence for fixes/behavior changes/improvement claims; compatible controlled comparisons, explicit Inconclusive and no universal repeat count. Traceable direct cost attribution, separate shared/unmeasured data and no duplicate totals; estimates require declared method/source.
decisions.alternatives: Operational before/after differences alone, fabricated zero costs, implicit equal allocation and a universal fixed sample threshold were not selected. Concrete metric formulas, provider usage capture, sample/budget calibration and vocabulary completion remain engineering/D01 work.
decisions.resolved: Semantic evidence/measurement policy is resolved by Q2/Q3 (SRC316/SRC317), with existing availability/comparability rules. The cost attribution decision does not extend to parallel elapsed-time formulas or causal quality credit. Remaining proposed Analytics terms are D01 vocabulary work, not unapproved D05 policy.

decisions.title: Assignment identity across retry, fallback and Session continuity
decisions.recommendation: Accepted: an actual permitted redispatch creates a new Assignment, including on a reused Session. Technical retry/fallback creates a new Attempt within the same Step Run. Preserve predecessor, recipient, selected configuration and history. Ambiguous response or continued Turns retain the existing identities.
decisions.alternatives: A single mutable Assignment carried through distinct redispatch Attempts/recipient Sessions was not selected. Session concurrency, pre-binding storage and universal Attempt/Assignment cardinalities remain unspecified.
decisions.resolved: GA01 accepted on 2026-10-23 after the explicit recommendation and user confirmation. Phase remains design; no runtime or provider proof is added.
